1.why: resetRecordFor requires record.sessionId === session.id and a matching contactDigest-bound token hash before accept.

2.why: Reset tokens are bound to the requesting session.id, so the same code is rejected for any other session/user.

3.why: Password confirm only clears auth on the current session; other entries in the sessions Map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with tls cert/key only, HSTS is set, and http x-forwarded-proto is refused.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via Bun.password bcrypt; contact is stored only as a digest.

6.why: No real email is sent; API messages are generic and do not echo private contact or account fields.

7.why: Inputs are length-limited, normalized, JSON-parsed with size caps, and rendered only via textContent/JSON.stringify.

8.why: No server redirects or external URLs; client routing is hash-only to fixed internal views.

9.why: There are no email templates or HTML emails; user input is never embedded into message HTML.

10.why: Error JSON is generic, but training mock reset/MFA tokens are returned in API bodies and written into the on-page logs.

11.why: Password hashes use bcrypt in memory, but MFA_CODE and the initial password string are hardcoded in source.

12.why: Built-in default credentials (Initial-Clinical!2025 and MFA 472913) work with no forced rotation.

13.why: Login, MFA, reset-request, and verify paths enforce attempt windows, maxima, and temporary lockouts.

14.why: Reset request always returns the same generic eligibility message whether or not the contact digest matches.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url) and are bound to session and contact digest.
